prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Scope: acceptance–loading handoff; airline loading excluded. Baggage Control System (Velvet): authoritative identity/flight/screening/status; validates routes, preserves holds/assignments, authorizes original-path returns, records events/dispositions/alarms; flags missing/duplicate/delayed sequences. Flight Data Gateway (Lantern) supplies timestamped flight/destination/revision/connection data and Flight Cutoff Advisory; validates departures. Baggage Operations Supervisor (Tern) approves recovery/capacity/priorities/dispositions/holds; confirms restrictions, Chute Occupancy Note acceptance, exception ownership; stops unsafe induction. Concourse Zone Controller (Mosslight) controls readiness/capacity/lanes, produces Recovery Route Card, reports states/alarms; screening bypass forbidden. Security Duty Manager resolves security/access holds, verifies Custody Seal Log. Explosives Response Team (Pebble) secures/assesses events, directs handling, produces log/communicates disposition. Maintenance Technician isolates energy/verifies stopped motion before entry; repairs/reports faults/restrictions, consults card/verifies Calibration Witness Tag; guards/approved bypass mandatory. Pier 4 Bag-Drop Unit sends Oversize Exception Ticket: approved routing required. Bag Tag Printer produces durable unique tags/Calibration Witness Tag; replacements authorized. Transfer Bag Feeder sends Late Transfer Bag Card; requires verified identity/onward flight and screening confirmation. Induction Tray Conveyor requires readable identity/routing/spacing/interlocks; unexpected stops prohibit entry. North Gate Scanner (Kestrel) captures tags; South Gate Scanner produces Manual Rescan Receipt; faults hold feed. Image Resolution Desk/Operator records image/receipt/ticket dispositions; inconclusive evidence requires inspection. Bag Reconciliation Station sends Bag Match Query, compares expected flight population, flags missing/duplicate/unmatched/count discrepancies. Airline Ramp Coordinator reviews query; verifies readable identity/current assignment/security release. Outbound Load Control Desk accepts loading record only with consistent assignment/reconciled count/status; unexplained physical-record differences block acceptance. Primary Crossbelt Sorter (Juniper) sends Chute Occupancy Note; routes cleared assignments/diverts exceptions. Secondary Inspection Chute excludes unrelated bags. East Make-Up Conveyor/West Make-Up Conveyor require reconciliation/access controls; East guards/capacity/identity checks. Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit. Orchard: unresolved identity; requires screening/destination validity. Restart: accounted bags/approved changes/personnel-clear/guards/understood-alarms/available-route. Departure: recorded screening

New part:
S238: The Transfer Bag Feeder is monitored for feed rate, interruptions, and backlog against its scheduled demand.
S239: The Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit is monitored for operating state, accumulation, and the time required to clear assigned work.
S240: The East Make-Up Conveyor and the West Make-Up Conveyor are assessed separately so that a local fault does not obscure the condition of the other conveyor.
S241: Tern reviews the operating dashboard and confirms that material service degradation has been assigned an owner and response priority.
S242: The Maintenance Technician investigates equipment faults that exceed the approved recovery interval and records the corrective action taken.
S243: The Security Duty Manager assesses any condition that could compromise screening coverage, security controls, or custody continuity.
S244: The Explosives Response Team is escalated to when an unresolved security condition requires its response under airport procedures.
S245: Service measures include availability, bags processed per operating interval, queue age, screening completion, and unresolved reconciliation differences.
S246: Thresholds and reporting intervals are established in the approved operating plan and reviewed against demand, flight schedules, and safety constraints.
S247: A degraded mode may be used only when the remaining equipment and procedures preserve required screening, traceability, custody, and reconciliation controls.
S248: Operations must suspend the affected activity when required controls cannot be maintained or when an unverified equipment state could misroute baggage.
S249: The Baggage Operations Supervisor coordinates escalation to maintenance, security, and airline operations according to the severity and operational impact of the condition.
S250: Return to service requires the fault to be corrected, required functional checks to pass, alarms to clear, and affected records to be reconciled.
S251: The responsible operational and technical personnel confirm that screening and custody controls are effective before normal routing resumes.
S252: The recovery is monitored at increased frequency until performance is stable and outstanding exceptions have been resolved or formally assigned.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
